cards.explanation: The answer is that serving God gets them nothing. They said, “It is futile to serve God. What have we gained by keeping His requirements…” It's like working overtime all month and then staring at your paycheck with your lip poked out. The LORD heard every word of it.

The answer is True, and it's a rough one. In verse 15 the people say, “So now we call the arrogant blessed.” They went and said it out loud. Then they said evildoers prosper and even test God and escape.

The scroll is about those who feared the LORD and honored His name. It was written “…regarding those who feared the LORD and honored His name.” They spoke with one another, the LORD listened and heard, and then the scroll was written before Him. Somebody got a whole record made, friends. Not even my cookie box gets that kind of paperwork.

The answer is that He will spare them like a man spares his son. The LORD says, “…I will spare them as a man spares his own son who serves him.” A son who serves his father, friends. That's the picture He picked. I'd say that's about as close as a picture gets.

The word is righteous, friends. The LORD says, “So you will again distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, between those who serve God and those who do not.” Those two pairs sit side by side. After all that talk about the arrogant being called blessed, He says you'll see the difference again.

The answer is the arrogant and every evildoer. The LORD says “…all the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble…” I think this one is heavy, friends, so I'll just read it plainly. He also says “Not a root or branch will be left to them.”

The answer is the sun of righteousness. The LORD says, “…the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings…” It's for those who fear His name. I love that the picture here is healing, friends. A sunrise after all that stubble talk.

The word is leap! The LORD says, “…you will go out and leap like calves from the stall.” Picture the door swinging open and everybody bouncing out. I can hop and dive face-first into the chocolate chips, gold base and all, but these folks do it way better.

The answer is the law of His servant Moses. The LORD says, “Remember the law of My servant Moses, the statutes and ordinances I commanded him for all Israel at Horeb.” Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10). The word is remember, friends, and it's for all Israel.

The answer is Elijah the prophet. The LORD says, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.” He sends him before the Day comes. That's a prophet showing up ahead of the main event.

Fathers goes in the first blank, and children goes in the second. The LORD says Elijah “…will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children…” That's a heart turning toward the children, friends. Then the verse says, “…and the hearts of the children to their fathers.” So it goes both directions, with hearts turning toward each other.
